newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil nine-month insurance premiums at $10.5 bln.
newsitem.headline: Brazil nine-month insurance premiums at $10.5 bln.

text.p: Brazilian insurance premiums in 1996's first nine months rose four percent to 10.8 billion reais ($10.5 billion) over the same period in 1995, said state insurance watchdog Susep.
Susep said in a statement that car insurance accounted for 30.28 percent of all premiums, while health and life insurance accounted for 18.57 and 19.59 percent, respectively.
Retained claims rose 19.45 percent between January and September to 6.4 billion reais ($6.2 billion) from 5.3 billion reais ($5.2 billion) in the same period a year ago, it said.

Technical provisions totalled 7.9 billion reais ($7.7 billion), of which 26.4 percent was invested in fixed-income assets, 15.3 percent in variable-income assets, 21.41 percent in real estate and 36.89 percent in public titles, Susep said.
